outcome: #577 complete: the environment field has locals and if/elif/else
owner_impact: Last part of the one-grammar work. environmental_scalar(x, y, config) can now use local variables, += and if/elif/else on comparisons and and/or/not, e.g. compute a distance once and return different values inside and outside a site. It stays a pure function of position: every path must return a number, with no loops, randomness or effects. Fields written as a single return compile to exactly the same simulator input as before, so no Experiment changed. With this, #577 is complete: all four code artifacts share one grammar. Test now: optional. To try it, write an environment field with an if/else in a copy of an Experiment and run it.

next.text: #577 (one grammar) is complete and closed. What remains from this thread is your audit of all Experiments, whenever you want it.

technical_evidence: Environment compiler on the shared statement parser with type, definite-assignment and definite-return checks; IR vlab.environment-scalar-ir/0.2 (body of statements) only when the body is more than a single return, else the unchanged 0.1 expression.
Rust EnvironmentRuntime accepts 0.1 and 0.2, validates types, definite assignment and definite return, evaluates both sides of and/or.

Equivalence: only compileEnvironmentScalar cases changed, none that previously compiled; changes are rejections by the old single-return rule (now accepted or given a specific error) and sharper errors on invalid input. New recorded reference 'environment-statements': native and WebAssembly bit-identical; the six other references unchanged.
